entries.purpose: 'Weekly Contest' event lettering (EN): yellow 'Weekly' + white 'Contest' in a blue outline with a cyan rim and a blue extrusion
entries.notes: missing-3d: SPEC-ui 4.2 lists it as B1 (a SwiftUI EventLogo with live text). Built here as a raster PER LANGUAGE (this EN file + weeklyContestLogoTR) from the game's OFL font (design/fonts/PCDisplay-Black.ttf, per-char tracking -0.9 pt) with the measured layer stack -- the lettering is the art, like logoArrowOut. If the shell prefers live text, the layer recipe (m3d_events.build_weekly_logo) ports 1:1 to a SwiftUI EventLogo. Frame 277 x 54 (SPEC-ui said 50: the 'y' descender + outline + extrusion reach y 245) at (60, 193.5). SELF-GRADE B: the phone's letters are a rounder, taller-x-height face; ours are PC Display.

entries.purpose: full-screen frost frame of the hourglass (freeze) booster: streaky cyan ice at the edges, a translucent white haze inward, thin white ice cracks, sparkles and tiny snowflakes; transparent middle
entries.screen: Level screen while the freeze runs
entries.notes: missing-3d: painted in code (value noise + random-walk cracks; no 3D model), built by m3d_make. SPEC-ui 4.2 proposed a code vignette (A) + a 120 pt crack tile (B2, the missing-svg lane's frostCracks); this one full-screen raster reproduces 065 in one texture and ALREADY CONTAINS cracks along every edge: use it ALONE, or the code vignette + frostCracks, never both. Draw it between the board and the HUD (065: the HUD and boosters stay crisp above the frost); fade in/out per SPEC-motion-audio. SELF-GRADE B: the phone's ice band is a little more saturated at the sides and its crack pattern denser in the corners.
